brief: The note argues the 2026 macro backdrop has peaked. The equity market has downgraded its growth outlook as financial conditions stop boosting GDP, and this fading tailwind is showing up in results: Q3 EPS beats moderated to 53% beating consensus by more than a standard deviation, down from a 64% four-quarter average, and revision breadth has declined. GS expects 2027 EPS growth to decelerate, with its estimate 7% below bottom-up consensus. From there the note raises concentration risk: non-AI S&P 500 EPS will grow only 4% next year while AI names drive 78% of 2027 earnings growth (Morgan Stanley), and the AI capex boom has transferred free cash flow from hyperscalers to semis (BofA). If that theme wobbles, Apollo's SHOK scenario models global credit spreads widening 10-30bps, US investment falling 1-4%, and South Korean exports falling 1-3%, phased from Q4 2026 through Q4 2027. Separately, forward P/E has already de-rated about 20% (23.2x to 18.7x) and global inflation is rising. The note's framing: conditions aren't bad yet, just incrementally less good, and markets dislike the period right after peak.
